name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,519

clue.text: Head of family's ordeal cut short during demonstration

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter of the word for ordeal is dropped
one thing happening during another sits inside it, so the shortened word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a protest march is a public demonstration
a trial is a painful ordeal

explanation.surface: A family's head is having a rough time, her ordeal interrupted by a street protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the woman who rules a family or clan, its female head.

clue.text: A small actress finally admitted to unconventional drama school

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that comes before it
unconventional means not in the usual form, so the word after it is rearranged
letters admitted to something are let inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the final letter of actress

explanation.surface: A minor actress finally gets a place at an offbeat drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama school' reads as one phrase, but drama is anagram fodder and school alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrassa is an Islamic religious college or teaching institution, so it is a kind of school.

clue.text: Twickenham's first comedian embracing northern regional accent

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the place name before it
to embrace something is to hold it in your arms, so one word wraps around a letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of Twickenham
a wag is a joker or comic person
N is the standard abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A comic from Twickenham, a London suburb famous for rugby, has a distinctive northern accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive nasal or local quality in someone's speech, a recognisable way of talking.

clue.text: Cognoscenti confused senile litigant

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the following two words are mixed into new order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doddery old person bringing a lawsuit leaves the experts baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the educated, cultured class of people who consider themselves expert judges of art and ideas.

clue.text: Secrecy clearly surrounding a way to combat consumerism?

definitions.note: a noun phrase defining a verb; the question mark flags the loose fit

indicators.note: the opening words are said to surround the answer, which sits inside them across the word gap

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Keeping things secret is presented as an obvious tactic against a shopping-mad society.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden in secRECY CLEarly.
explanation.definitionFit: Reusing materials instead of buying new goods is a means of resisting a throwaway, purchase-driven culture.

clue.text: Drug in dish is heroin

blocks.note: hash is a dish of chopped meat and potato
taken as written
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A warning that a meal has been laced with heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like a hiding place for the answer, but it is a synonym, not the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is cannabis resin, a narcotic smoked or eaten for its effects.

clue.text: Far out old hairstyle

indicators.note: out here means wrong or out of place, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: 'Far out' is sixties slang praising a retro haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far out' reads as one hippie exclamation, but out is the anagram signal working on far.
explanation.definitionFit: An afro is a rounded, bushy natural style of tightly curled hair, popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Instrument in standard box turned up broken by leader of orchestra

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the word for box is reversed
the leader of a word is its first letter
a word broken by something has that thing inserted into it, splitting it

blocks.note: a standard is a banner or flag
the box and the tele are both informal words for a television set
the opening letter of orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestral instrument is kept in a box that is upended and damaged by the concertmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small wind instrument like a recorder, a kind of whistle flute.

clue.text: Old Scottish monster eschewing top of Scottish garment

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter
to eschew is to avoid or go without, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
the nickname of the Loch Ness monster
the first letter of the second Scottish in the clue

explanation.surface: An old monster from Scotland refuses to wear the top half of its Scottish outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A onesie is a loose one-piece suit covering body, arms and legs, worn for lounging or sleep.

clue.text: Pair help to mix adhesive for operation

indicators.note: mixing jumbles things together, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
cement is a glue or binding substance

explanation.surface: Two people lend a hand stirring glue together for some job.
explanation.walkthrough: Cement is also the bone cement surgeons use to fix the new joint, so the wordplay hints at the procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip replacement is a surgical procedure swapping a damaged joint for an artificial one.

clue.text: Doctor behind plan

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A doctor is the one secretly behind some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position signal for placing one piece after another, but it supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline of a scheme, so it can mean a plan.

clue.text: Criticise players getting one wicket

blocks.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
I is the Roman numeral for one
a wicket is a small gate or door

explanation.surface: A cricket team is criticised for only taking one wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'wicket' paint a cricket scene, but players are actors and wicket is the old word for a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke or reprimand someone severely, a stronger form of finding fault.

clue.text: Innocent lass meeting setter during party

indicators.note: something taking place during another sits within it, so these pieces go inside the word for party

blocks.note: gel is a jokey upper-class pronunciation of girl
the setter refers to themself as I
the ANC is the African National Congress, a South African political party

explanation.surface: A young woman runs into the crossword setter at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic describes someone pure, sweet and sinless, like an angel, hence blameless and innocent.

clue.text: Person from the Middle East airs broadcast by priest

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters of the preceding word are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern figure appears on the radio alongside a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airs broadcast' looks like a radio phrase, but broadcast scrambles airs.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Relative, male, scoring point at the Spanish religious building

blocks.note: sis is short for sister
a tine is a prong or sharp point, as on a fork or antler
a chap is a man
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sister and a man score a point against the Spanish, as in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' places the man's piece after the point: he scores it and stands beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sistine Chapel is the papal chapel in the Vatican, a famous place of worship painted by Michelangelo.

clue.text: Discharge soldiers in part of platoon

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: a section is a subdivision of an army platoon
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British army

explanation.surface: An army order to dismiss some troops within a unit of the platoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads as a military verb for releasing soldiers, but it is the noun for something oozed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretion is a substance released by a gland or organ, a bodily emission.

clue.text: Book given to so-called academic's parents

indicators.note: so-called hints that the word is only what it is called, i.e. how it sounds, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain; the possessive is read as a plural sound

explanation.surface: A book is handed to the parents of a so-called academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeders produce offspring, so they are animals or people acting as mothers and fathers.

clue.text: Mobile camera for capturing dessert ingredient?

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the next two words shift into a new order
letters that capture something hold it prisoner inside them

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a tart is a sweet pastry pudding

explanation.surface: A phone camera is used to snap a pudding, perhaps for a food blog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dessert ingredient?' reads as the definition, but dessert does double duty as wordplay; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream of tartar is potassium bitartrate, a powder used in baking to stabilise egg whites and raise cakes.

clue.text: Grain scattered in drained marshes' borders

indicators.note: scattered things are strewn about, so the word before it is jumbled
a drained word is emptied of its contents, leaving just its outside letters
in places the jumbled letters inside the outer shell

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first and last letters of marshes

explanation.surface: Seed is strewn along the edges of reclaimed wetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Margins are edges or rims around something, the same as its edges or boundaries.

clue.text: Fellow judged ready for the post

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
to rank is to rate or grade

explanation.surface: A man is assessed as suitable for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The post' suggests a job vacancy; it is the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A franked letter has been stamped by a machine to show postage is paid, so it can be mailed.

clue.text: Line on map is over bank at mouth of river

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
a bar is a sandbank across a river mouth

explanation.surface: A description of a map line running over a riverbank at an estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a contour on a weather chart joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Top Swedish diner

blocks.note: Sw. is a dictionary abbreviation for Swedish
a diner is someone eating a meal

explanation.surface: Praise for the best restaurant in Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective praising the diner; it is the clothing sense, a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted jumper worn on the upper body, so it is an item of upper clothing.

clue.text: Film shown in great exhibition space

blocks.note: ace means excellent
the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain

explanation.surface: A movie is screened at a splendid gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but it is the plastic sheeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a cellulose plastic made into thin transparent sheets, as used for photographic stock.

clue.text: Three notes given to Oriana's first mate

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the name before it

blocks.note: three musical notes: A, MI from the sol-fa scale, and G
the opening letter of Oriana

explanation.surface: A first mate is offered a little tune by a woman named Oriana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' reads as a ship's officer, but first belongs to Oriana.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a pal or buddy.

clue.text: False alibi's bad when editor's leaving special field of interest

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the next word is rearranged into something else
something leaving has gone away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
wicked means evil or bad
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A fake alibi is a poor idea once the newspaper editor has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiwick was a bailiff's district, and figuratively means one's own area of expertise or domain.

clue.text: Enamel item contains cream

indicators.note: the words before it are said to contain the answer, which lies within them across the gap

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An enamelled object has cream inside it, maybe a decorated jug.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden in enamEL ITEm.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, just as the elite are the best of a group.

clue.text: Cuts edges off carved letter

indicators.note: taking the edges off removes the outside letters, first and last

blocks.note: to prune is to cut back

explanation.surface: Someone trims the edges off a letter they have carved.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuts is a verb here, so the synonym is in its verb form too.
explanation.definitionFit: A rune is a character of the old Germanic alphabets, typically cut into stone or wood.

clue.text: Idiots use mobile, causing public disorder

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the preceding words shift into a new order

blocks.note: all nine letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fools use their phones to stir up rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' reads as a phone; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech or action incites people to rebel against authority, stirring up unrest.
